subject: Deployment readiness: throughput benchmark and unit-econ breakdown for LedgerOps MAP
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Simmons <j.simmons@ledgerops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment readiness: throughput benchmark and unit-econ breakdown for LedgerOps MAP

Jordan —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion I sketched a focused MAP entry that covers the throughput benchmarking and unit-econ analysis LedgerOps asked for. Goal is to validate performance and give procurement a clear cost picture ahead of the POC. High level:

- Objectives:
  - Verify sustained throughput (tokens/sec and sustained QPS) at target concurrency.
  - Measure tail latency and TTFT for common request shapes.
  - Produce unit-econ summary: $/1k tokens, $/s of GPU at target throughput, and projected monthly spend at expected load.

- Success criteria (examples):
  - Sustained QPS >= 120 rps for the 2k-token median request shape with 95th p99 latency < 600ms.
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token) < 120ms at target concurrency.
  - Unit cost per 1k input tokens < $0.018 (baseline target; we’ll refine after runs).

- Proposed test matrix (draft):
  - Models: redwood-13B-quant / redwood-7B-quant (compare).
  - Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 64, 128 concurrent connections.
  - Sequence lengths: 256 / 512 / 2048 tokens.
  - Prefix caching: on/off.
  - Warmup: 15-minute warmup per point; 30-minute sustained sample per steady-state point.

- Measurements to produce:
  - tokens/sec, sustained QPS (sample windows), median/p95/p99 latency, TTFT distribution, payload size distribution, token breakdown (input vs generated).
  - Unit econ calc: measured tokens/sec -> GPU $/s -> $/1k tokens mapping; scenario scaling for 50k, 250k, 1M monthly requests.

Asks for you: can you confirm the workload shapes (short/medium/long) and share a sanitized trace or 100 representative requests? Also confirm preferred test window — we’re proposing the week of Nov 9 to Nov 13.

I attached a draft schedule and the minimal dataset template (see attachments). If that window works I’ll lock in the MAP milestones and loop infra (Ben/Marissa) for the run.

Thanks,

Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: MAP_deployment_schedule.docx

From: Jordan Simmons <j.simmons@ledgerops.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: LedgerOps Eng Team <eng-team@ledgerops.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment readiness: throughput benchmark and unit-econ breakdown for LedgerOps MAP

Ava —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the three shapes: short (~128 tokens), medium (~512 tokens), long (~2k tokens). I uploaded a sanitized sample of 150 request traces to the Drive folder and attached a small CSV with observed request rates. We prefer the week of Nov 9; Nov 10–11 are best for our infra folks.

A couple of constraints to flag: we must enforce a 30-day data retention policy on any traces you keep for analysis, and any logs with PII must be redacted. Procurement asked for an SOW and indicative monthly cost estimate before signing — if you can include a high-level $/month for the three load scenarios that would help.

Jordan Simmons
Head of Platform, LedgerOps
j.simmons@ledgerops.com | +1 (312) 555-4410

Attachments: ledgerops_sample_traces.zip

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Deployment readiness: throughput benchmark and unit-econ breakdown for LedgerOps MAP

Team —

Looping you in on LedgerOps MAP. Jordan confirmed the workload shapes and prefers Nov 10–11 for the runs. I drafted a compact MAP with goals, acceptance criteria, and deliverables (PDF in Drive). Key asks for the run:

1) Measurement infra: we’ll use the Redwood test harness (gatling-like runner) against a Dedicated instance (configured per Ben’s note below). Collect token-level timing and export raw traces to the shared Drive.

2) Measurement steps (short):
   - Cluster warmup: 15 min at 50% target QPS.
   - Baseline run: single-connection throughput @ each sequence length.
   - Concurrency sweep with steady-state 30-min windows.
   - Stress run to find graceful degradation point (increase concurrency until 20% drop in success).

3) Metrics to deliver in MAP artifact:
   - tokens/sec and sustained QPS table (per sequence length + concurrency).
   - TTFT and p95/p99 latency by request shape.
   - Unit econ spreadsheet mapping measured tokens/sec to $/1k tokens and monthly cost scenarios.

I attached the schedule and the initial unit economics assumptions (see attachments). Ben/ Priyom — can you confirm the instance sizing and cold-start vs warm cache plan? I propose we hand the SOW draft to Jordan by Nov 12 so procurement has it ahead of their PO cycle.

Ava

Attachments: unit_econ_breakdown_v1.xlsx, MAP_deployment_schedule.docx, sustained_qps_plot.png

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Deployment readiness: throughput benchmark and unit-econ breakdown for LedgerOps MAP

Agree with the plan. A few technical decisions and estimated numbers to seed the unit-econ sheet:

- Hardware: Dedicated pool with 4x A100 80GB (mixed precision path); model: redwood-13B-quant.
- Runtime tuning: batch size 16 for medium/long, continuous KV caching enabled for prefix-heavy flows.
- Warm-up: 15 min; we will run a 30-min steady-state sample per concurrency point.
- Measurement infra: tracer exports token timestamps; we’ll compute tokens/sec over 1s and 60s windows and report sustained QPS as the 60s rolling mean at steady state.

Quick unit-econ back-of-envelope (assumptions in sheet):
- GPU cost assumption: $3.60 / GPU-hour effective (after discounts).
- If we measure sustained 20k tokens/sec on the cluster, that maps to ~72M tokens/hour -> ~0.018 $/1k tokens (matches baseline target).
- Projected monthly cost at 100k daily requests (median 512 tokens) ~ $7.2k/month (model/quantization dependent).

I attached updated unit_econ_breakdown_v1.xlsx with formula cells and the plotting code behind sustained_qps_plot.png. Priyom — please confirm the runbook steps and whether we should capture the cold-start TTFT separately in the SOW.

-Ben

Attachment: unit_econ_breakdown_v1.xlsx

From: Jordan Simmons <j.simmons@ledgerops.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment readiness: throughput benchmark and unit-econ breakdown for LedgerOps MAP

Ava/Team —

This looks good and aligns with what procurement needs. Two final asks before Nov 10 run:

1) Please send a one-page MAP summary (objectives, acceptance criteria, schedule) we can attach to our internal approval.
2) We’ll need a short SOW + DocuSign for the POC (term: 30 days, predefined run windows, redaction & retention terms). Procurement contact: procurement@ledgerops.com.

If you can push those docs by EOD Nov 12 we should be able to sign and provide a PO before the run. Confirmed run window: Nov 10–11 (LedgerOps infra team on call).

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Jordan
Head of Platform, LedgerOps
procurement@ledgerops.com
